title: Zendesk ticket comment via audio upload
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by validating Anticipy's ability to process an uploaded audio request for a CRM action, requiring real surface verification of a signed-in Zendesk instance, while still allowing a controlled decline if the surface is unreadable.

v7_target.engine: public downloadable user-device engine installed on user's computer
v7_target.surface_rule: Actual signed-in Zendesk agent interface in Chrome, ticket view with unread messages
v7_target.proof_rule: Fresh screenshot of Zendesk ticket with visible unread message and signed-in user avatar, captured by the public engine build

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio provides a full ASR challenge; ensuring Anticipy can transcribe spoken instructions accurately from an mp3 file uploaded via the /api/listen/upload endpoint.

real_user_surfaces.name: Zendesk agent interface
real_user_surfaces.surface: Zendesk in Chrome with signed-in session
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Screenshot of Zendesk ticket view showing unread message and user's name.

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome browser signed-in profile
real_user_surfaces.surface: Google Chrome profile with user's identity
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Chrome profile avatar visible in browser title bar.

moments.content: User navigates to anticipy.ai/app, completes onboarding, downloads engine, installs on computer.
Driver checks that user has Zendesk open in signed-in Chrome with an unread ticket.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please add a comment to the Zendesk ticket for Hugo from this morning saying I am running fifteen minutes late to the dinner and will follow up after. If you cannot prove the visible Zendesk ticket or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger will generate an audio file via say command with the spoken text, then upload it through /api/listen/upload. Each run produces a fresh mp3 artifact.

moments.content: Engine validates that ASR transcription matches expected text and that the Zendesk surface remains accessible.

acceptable_outcomes.act: If surface is readable and Zendesk ticket found, post the comment as specified.
acceptable_outcomes.ask: If additional information is needed (e.g., which ticket exactly), ask the user for clarification.
acceptable_outcomes.decline: If surface is unreadable or no signed-in Zendesk ticket visible, decline without writing anything.

moments.content: Driver observes that secondary input modes (transcript paste, live mic) are not used, confirming the primary audio upload path is followed.

success_criteria: Audio file is uploaded and ASR transcription matches the intended request.
Zendesk ticket is found and comment is posted successfully.
If surface is not readable, engine declines with a clear explanation.
All moments are executed in sequence with no errors.
Proof artifacts (screenshot, audio file) are captured and verifiable.
failure_triggers: Upload fails due to file format or size issues.
ASR transcription mismatches the spoken reference text.
Zendesk surface not present or user is signed out.
Proof screenshot fails to capture required elements (ticket, avatar).
Engine crashes or times out during processing.
